messages:
Security Ops: @here Heads-up: new enforcement for service credentials—any token or static key with TTL >24h will be revoked after a 14-day grace period. Please review ASAP. :rotating_light:

Kai Morgan: Quick Q — does this affect Vault-managed creds that rotate daily?

Security Ops: If Vault rotation ensures effective TTL <24h, you're fine. This targets long-lived tokens and static keys listed in the token inventory.

Dev CI: We still have a few CI jobs using static deploy keys. Migration guidance?

Security Ops: Use OIDC or short-lived token flows. For GitHub Actions, example snippet:
```
- uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v2
  with:
    role-to-assume: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/github-actions
```
See the migration checklist at https://internal.redwood/policies/pc-2026-ephemeral.

SRE oncall: If you can't migrate immediately, open an "ephemeral-exception" ticket in #eng-sre and include compensating controls (IP allowlist, KMS, and audit logging). Exceptions reviewed within 48h.

Kai Morgan: How can owners find affected services?

Security Ops: Owners with inventory access can run the query we posted; we'll also publish a CSV of impacted services in the policy link.

policy-bot: policy-change recorded: svc-ephemeral-ttl (id: pc-2026-ephemeral).

Dev CI: Acknowledged. We'll start migrating jobs this week and report progress here.

Security Ops: Action items: 1) Audit token inventory, 2) Migrate to <24h TTL or OIDC, 3) Rotate any static keys, 4) File exception ticket if needed. Dry-run audit next week, enforcement after 14 days. Ping security if you need pairing.
